stories.title: HMRC Publishes Guidance on Short-Term Business Visitors (GfC19)
stories.summary: HMRC published GfC19, the latest in its Guidelines for Compliance series, to help UK employers and overseas workers understand tax obligations when employees perform duties in the UK on a short-term basis. The guidance sets out best practice examples and compliance expectations for short-term business visitor arrangements.

stories.title: HMRC to Begin Signing Up MTD 'No-Shows' from September 2026
stories.summary: HMRC has announced it will start signing up taxpayers who have not yet registered for Making Tax Digital (MTD) beginning September 2026. Those eligible will be identified using information HMRC already holds and contacted by post or through their Personal Tax Account.

stories.title: Asylum Appeals Target Launched for Faster Removals
stories.summary: The Home Office has introduced a new 24-week target for asylum and immigration appeal decisions, down from the current 67-week average. The measure is expected to speed up removal of those with no right to be in the UK and contribute to estimated taxpayer savings of £6.9 billion.

stories.title: Thirteen Asylum Hotels Exited and Returned to Local Communities
stories.summary: The Home Office announced that 13 more asylum hotels have been exited and returned to their communities, with fewer than 170 now in use — down from a peak of 400 in 2023. The government aims to close every asylum hotel by the end of this parliament.

stories.title: Detention Services Orders Updated
stories.summary: The Home Office published updated Detention Services Orders, providing guidance for the management and operation of immigration detention facilities.

stories.title: UK Continues Crackdown on Russia with Tough New Sanctions
stories.summary: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced the UK's first major Russia sanctions package under his tenure, targeting 19 entities including six Russian banks, six shadow fleet tankers, and four companies importing rare metals used for military equipment. The UK has now sanctioned over 3,400 individuals and entities under its Russia sanctions regime.

stories.title: Russia Warns UK Over British-Made Drones Used in Ukraine Strikes
stories.summary: Russia's embassy issued a warning to the UK after British-made drones were confirmed to have been used in strikes on targets inside Russia, including refineries and logistics centres. The MoD responded by reaffirming the UK stands 'shoulder to shoulder' with Ukraine in its defence against Putin's illegal invasion.

stories.title: Free Bus Travel 24/7 for Disabled People Announced
stories.summary: The Prime Minister announced that from April 2027, eligible disabled people across England will be able to travel on buses for free at any time of day, removing existing time restrictions on concessionary passes. The £60 million initiative is backed by DWP (£40m) and the Department for Transport (£20m).

stories.title: Government Announces £65 Million Drought Support Package for Farmers
stories.summary: DEFRA announced a £65 million support package for farmers in England in response to the ongoing drought, including an additional £50 million for the Sustainable Farming Incentive 2026, up to £15 million for on-farm reservoirs, and temporary scheme flexibilities to allow farmers to manage dry conditions without losing payments.

stories.title: Drought Order Applications Filed Across England and Wales
stories.summary: With much of England officially in drought, formal applications for Drought Orders have been submitted in multiple regions, with DEFRA and the Environment Agency facilitating access to additional water resources for farmers while maintaining environmental protections.

stories.title: Russia Warns UK After British-Made Drones Strike Targets Inside Russia
stories.summary: Russia issued a stark warning to the UK after British-made drones were confirmed used in strikes on Russian targets including refineries and Wildberries logistics centres, causing an estimated £35 billion in economic damage. The MoD reaffirmed the UK's commitment to providing Ukraine with the equipment it needs to defend itself.

stories.title: UK Defence Innovation Security Open Call 2026 Cycle 1 Launched
stories.summary: UK Defence Innovation (UKDI) launched its Security Open Call 2026 Cycle 1, inviting proposals that address security challenges through innovation. The programme is one of UKDI's key funding competition mechanisms.

stories.title: Lanarkshire AI Growth Zone Secures £300 Million Investment as Dell Establishes Scottish Base
stories.summary: The UK Government announced a landmark £300 million financing package for DataVita to expand the Lanarkshire AI Growth Zone, backed by a £202 million National Wealth Fund guarantee. Dell Technologies will also establish its Scottish team at Lanarkshire's AI Innovation Park, with the development expected to support more than 3,400 jobs.

stories.title: NHS Losing Public Trust in Its Data Abilities, Research Warns
stories.summary: New research from NHS Alliance and Understanding Patient Data reveals public confidence in the NHS's ability to protect health data has fallen from 58% to 52% in the past year, with 44% concerned about unauthorised data access. Despite concerns, 89% of people support health data use in some circumstances, but 61% say they know little about how it is used.

stories.title: Over a Quarter of NHS Staff Lose More Than 10 Hours a Week to Admin
stories.summary: A YouGov survey commissioned by NHS Shared Business Services found 28% of NHS staff spend more than 10 hours weekly on administrative tasks — equivalent to 220,000 full-time roles or 430 million hours annually. Over 92% also deal with inefficient or duplicated processes each week, with 51% reporting increased stress or burnout as a result.

stories.title: People with Severe Intellectual Disabilities Live 24 Years Shorter on Average
stories.summary: A new study published in The Guardian found that people with severe intellectual disabilities die 24 years younger on average than the wider population, with 40% of such deaths considered potentially avoidable. The findings raise serious questions about the adequacy of NHS care and support for this group.

stories.title: Slough Postal Fraud Firm Ordered to Repay £1m to Royal Mail
stories.summary: Global Express Worldwide Ltd, based in Slough, has been ordered by Southwark Crown Court to repay £1,071,878 to Royal Mail after being convicted of fraud conspiracy as part of a nine-year postal scam that cost Royal Mail an estimated £70 million. The firm made more than £3 million from the criminal activity.
